question: Nagaur was conquered and annexed by which house of Rajputs during late Mughal period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jodhpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Nagaur**, a prominent region in Rajasthan, was conquered and annexed by the **Jodhpur state** during the late Mughal period.

• The rulers of Jodhpur belonged to the **Rathore clan of Rajputs**, who were known for their valor and strategic political maneuvers.

• During the late Mughal period, the central authority of the Mughal Empire weakened, creating opportunities for regional powers like Jodhpur to expand their territories.

• The Rathores of Jodhpur annexed Nagaur to solidify their control over Rajasthan and to check the influence of rival Rajput clans and neighboring kingdoms.

• This strategic acquisition played a significant role in enhancing the political and economic influence of Jodhpur in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Jodhpur State (Marwar):**

• Jodhpur, also known as Marwar, was one of the largest and most powerful princely states in Rajasthan.

• The Rathores established their dominance over this region in the 13th century and played a significant role in Rajput politics.

• Its strategic location in the Thar Desert made it a critical trade and cultural hub during medieval times.

• **Nagaur:**

• Nagaur, historically an important region, was known for its fertile plains and served as a strategic location connecting different parts of Rajasthan.

• It was contested by various Rajput clans and the Mughals due to its geographic and economic significance.

• The annexation of Nagaur by Jodhpur further strengthened the Rathore dynasty's influence in Rajasthan.

• **Decline of the Mughal Empire:**

• The decline of the Mughal Empire, particularly after the death of Emperor Aurangzeb in 1707, led to political instability in India.

• This allowed regional powers, including Rajput kingdoms like Jodhpur, to consolidate power and expand their territories.

• **Rathore Clan:**

• The Rathores are a prominent Rajput clan known for their martial traditions and governance.

• They ruled over Marwar (Jodhpur) and were influential in shaping the political landscape of Rajasthan.

• Key rulers like Rao Jodha, the founder of Jodhpur, and others left a lasting legacy in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Mewar:**

• Mewar, another prominent Rajput kingdom, was ruled by the Sisodia dynasty.

• It is historically known for its resistance against the Mughals, particularly under Maharana Pratap.

• Mewar did not annex Nagaur; its focus was primarily on defending its own territory.

• **Amber (Jaipur):**

• The Kachhwaha dynasty ruled Amber and later Jaipur.

• They were known for their alliances with the Mughals, particularly under Raja Man Singh.

• Amber did not have control over Nagaur during the late Mughal period.

• **Bikaner:**

• Bikaner, ruled by the Rathore clan, was a smaller Rajput state compared to Jodhpur.

• Although it shared cultural and familial ties with Jodhpur, it did not annex Nagaur.
